entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cesare Alfieri di Sostegno, born into a distinguished Piedmontese noble family, was a pivotal Italian politician and diplomat whose career significantly intersected with the tumultuous early phases of the Risorgimento. While his exact birthdate remains obscure, his death on April 16, 1869, marks the conclusion of a life dedicated to the political and constitutional development of the Kingdom of Sardinia, which would eventually form the nucleus of a unified Italy. Alfieri distinguished himself as a moderate liberal, advocating for constitutional monarchy and diplomatic solutions amidst the fervent nationalist and revolutionary currents of the mid-19th century, thereby contributing to the gradual institutionalization of liberal principles in the burgeoning Italian state.

Alfieri's most prominent role came during the revolutionary year of 1848, when he briefly served as Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia from August 19 to October 11. His premiership coincided with a critical juncture of the First Italian War of Independence, following the initial Sardinian defeats. During this period, Alfieri navigated complex diplomatic challenges, including attempts to mediate a peace settlement with Austria and address the internal political divisions exacerbated by the war. Although his time as prime minister was short-lived, he remained an influential figure, serving as a senator for life in the Subalpine Parliament and later as president of the Senate, where he continued to champion constitutional reforms and moderate political discourse.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cesare Alfieri di Sostegno played a significant role in stabilizing the constitutional monarchy of the Kingdom of Sardinia during the volatile 1848 revolutions, directly influencing the early institutional development that led to Italian unification. His moderate policies helped secure liberal gains against both reactionary and radical forces.
